validity.researcher_notes: Starting from the sheet's own wiki citations (2 Business Standard articles + 1 Hindu BusinessLine article + 1 Economic Times article), all four resolve live and I read full text of each. EXISTENCE: unambiguous. In 2007-08 the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas authorized Relogistics Infrastructure Ltd (Relog), a subsidiary of Reliance Gas Transportation Infrastructure Ltd (RGTIL, 'a RIL group company' per Business Standard), to build four trunk gas pipelines totalling 2,175 km: Kakinada-Haldia, Kakinada-Chennai, Chennai-Tuticorin and Chennai-Bangalore-Mangalore. Kakinada-Haldia itself is independently and specifically named (not just swept into an aggregate figure) in three of the four citations: 'RIL firm may lose Kakinada-Haldia gas line project' (Business Standard, dateline Jan 21 2013) gives the route explicitly as 'the proposed 1,100-km pipeline from Kakinada in Andhra to Haldia in West Bengal'; 'Petroleum regulator wants Reliance Gas' pipeline licences cancelled' (Hindu BusinessLine, published 2012-06-05, verified via article:published_time meta tag) lists 'Kakinada-Haldia' by name among the four authorized RGTIL lines and describes PNGRB pushing for cancellation over a bank-guarantee/deadline dispute; 'RGTIL loses rights to lay gas pipelines' (Business Standard, dateline Jan 25 2013) confirms the government formally cancelled all four RGTIL authorizations, naming Kakinada-Haldia first in the list, citing RGTIL's own stated reason (falling KG-D6 output made the pipeline uneconomic). CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as a gas transmission trunk line -- explicitly called a 'trunk pipeline'/one of 'four trunk pipelines' in the sourcing, cross-state (Andhra Pradesh to West Bengal) at 1,100 km, not a gathering/feeder/CGD line. DUPLICATE CHECK against the roster's other 12 India-gas cancelled rows: none overlaps this corridor -- P0932 (Kakinada-Vizag-Srikakulam) runs north along the coast within Andhra Pradesh only, and P2752 (Kondalapalli-Tirupati) runs south; neither reaches West Bengal. Not a relabel of any other row. IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION NOTE (not a duplicate risk for P3342, but worth flagging for the record): the sheet's 4th wiki citation, an Economic Times article ('GAIL, ONGC to invest Rs 3,000 cr for pipeline project', dateline Feb 2 2007), describes a DIFFERENT, competing Kakinada-Haldia proposal -- a GAIL/ONGC 50-50 SPV building a 1,000-km pipeline via Peddapuram-Srikakulam-Bhubaneshwar-Cuttack-Kharagpur to Pandua near Kolkata, to move ONGC's own KG-DWN-98/2 gas, explicitly described in the same article as running 'almost parallel to a similar pipeline proposed by Reliance Industries.' P3342's Owner1=Reliance Industries Ltd (100%) confirms this GEM row tracks the RIL/RGTIL project, correctly, not the GAIL/ONGC one -- but the wiki page's own citation list conflates the two histories under one page, and I found no evidence the GAIL/ONGC SPV pipeline was ever separately built or tracked elsewhere in GEM. That is a scope question for a future Discovery pass on this corridor, not a P3342 defect.

validity.researcher_notes: Business Standard ('RGTIL loses rights...') states: 'Relogistics Infrastructure Ltd (Relog), a subsidiary of RGTIL, had in 2007-08 won the mandate to build these pipelines' and separately calls the parent 'Mukesh Ambani's privately held firm' (i.e. RGTIL, not the publicly listed RIL). The companion Business Standard article ('RIL firm may lose...') does link RGTIL to the RIL group explicitly: 'Reliance Gas Transportation Infrastructure Ltd (RGTIL), a RIL group company.' So attributing 100% ownership to 'Reliance Industries Ltd' is a reasonable simplification of a multi-tier private subsidiary chain (RIL group -> RGTIL -> Relog) rather than a fabricated or unrelated name, but it is not the literal entity named in any citation. Flagging as a caveat, not a hard concern, since I found nothing suggesting the pipeline belonged to any entity outside the Reliance/RIL group.
